## Overview

`WB_HartJohnstoneForestClassesAI_Sol6_1` converts LandR cohort biomass into a
six-class forest map. It adapts Hart et al. (2019), Table 1 and section 2.4
(p. 873), by using biomass in place of basal area and stem density. It is not a
literal implementation of that paper and does not use age, drainage, basal-area,
stem-density, or minimum-biomass forest thresholds.

## Inputs and output

The module requires `cohortData` with `pixelGroup`, `speciesCode`, and `B`, and
a single-layer `terra::SpatRaster` `pixelGroupMap`. It creates the labeled
integer raster `WB_HartJohnstoneForestClassesAI_Sol6_1_Map`; its geometry matches
`pixelGroupMap`.

The classifier can also be used without SpaDES:

```{r external-helper, eval=FALSE}
source("R/classifyHartJohnstoneForest.R")
forestClasses <- classifyHartJohnstoneForest(cohortData, pixelGroupMap)
```

It accepts a `data.frame` or `data.table`, resolves LandR taxonomy through
`utils::data()` without attaching LandR, and has no simulation dependency. The
helper neither writes files nor changes its inputs.

## Legend and adaptation rules

Biomass is summed across all cohorts and ages in a pixel group. All proportions
use recognized tree biomass in that group as the denominator, and $0.66$ is an
inclusive threshold.

| Value | Label | Assignment |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Deciduous | Broadleaf-deciduous biomass is at least 66% |
| 2 | Conifer–deciduous mix | Neither broadleaf deciduous nor all conifers is at least 66% |
| 3 | Conifer mix | All conifers are at least 66%; pine, larch, and spruce are each below 66% |
| 4 | Pine (jack pine + other pines) | Pooled pine biomass is at least 66% |
| 5 | Larch | Pooled larch biomass is at least 66% |
| 6 | Spruce | Pooled spruce biomass is at least 66% |

Pine is pooled at genus level, including jack and lodgepole pine; consequently,
class 4 is broader than a jack-pine-only class. Larch is coniferous. Single
pine/larch/spruce dominance is assigned before conifer mix. Class 3 is a
residual conifer class, so fir and other recognized conifers contribute to it
but are not relabeled spruce. This is a limitation of the western extension.

Cells whose map value is `0`, `NA`, or `NaN` are `NA` (NoData), not class 0.
The classifier stops for a missing raster, malformed IDs, positive map groups
without cohort records, zero group biomass, missing/non-finite/negative biomass,
or unknown species with positive biomass. An empty cohort table is allowed only
for a map containing no positive IDs. Cohort groups absent from the map are
ignored.

## Timing and files

Load after `Biomass_core`. The module initializes the in-memory output at the
simulation start, then classifies after the core succession work at every
positive `successionTimestep` boundary, using priority 8.5. It reads the
`Biomass_core` timestep rather than maintaining a separate classification
interval. The initial state is exported at simulation start (time 0 in the main
project), as well as at every positive succession boundary.

For each such update, the configured `outputPath` receives:

```text
WB_HartJohnstoneForestClassesAI_Sol6_1_Map_time_<simulation-time>.tif
WB_HartJohnstoneForestClassesAI_Sol6_1_Map_time_<simulation-time>.qml
```

Times are formatted to avoid rounding-name collisions. A collision or write
failure stops rather than replacing an earlier result. TIFFs retain integer
codes, labels, geometry, NoData, and the fixed palette. The matching QML uses a
paletted unique-values renderer with all six labels and colors, including absent
classes. If QGIS does not automatically apply it, load the same-basename QML
from **Layer Properties → Symbology → Style → Load Style**. Actual QGIS GUI
rendering remains unverified.

## Standalone demonstration mode

The module parameter `demoMode` defaults to `FALSE`. When explicitly enabled,
`.inputObjects` supplies deterministic synthetic data only for inputs not
reported by `suppliedElsewhere()`. With neither input supplied, a six-cell
EPSG:3005 map and cohorts illustrate all classes. Cohort-only runs receive a map
of their positive IDs; map-only runs receive example cohorts cycling six
compositions across positive IDs. Both supplied inputs are retained unchanged,
and incompatible inputs remain validation errors. The demonstration is static,
not a model of forest growth.

The core succession timestep takes precedence whenever present. Only in demo
mode, if that parameter is absent, `demoSuccessionTimestep` supplies the interval
(default 1 year). Invalid supplied core intervals are not masked. Informational
messages identify synthetic input creation and fallback use. Load only this
module for standalone demonstration and use a separate output directory;
positive timestep boundaries still write the same TIFF/QML output pairs.

## Testing

Set `HART_TEST_OUTPUT_DIR` to a new disposable directory, then run:

```{r run-tests, eval=FALSE}
source("tests/run-tests.R")
```

The focused tests cover all class rules and boundaries, validation, geometry,
non-mutation, succession synchronization, and TIFF/QML exports without a full
Biomass simulation.

## Reference

Hart, S. J., Henkelman, J., McLoughlin, P. D., Nielsen, S. E., Truchon-Savard, A.,
and Johnstone, J. F. (2019). Examining forest resilience to changing fire frequency
in a fire-prone region of boreal forest. Global Change Biology, 25, 869–884.
doi:10.1111/gcb.14550. Classification: Table 1 and section 2.4, p. 873.
